3.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

PUBLIC COMMENT RULES

“(California Government Code Section 54954.3).
(a) Every agenda for a special meeting shall provide an opportunity for members of the
public to directly address the legislative body on any item that has been described in the
notice for the meeting, before or during the legislative body’s consideration of the item,
that is within the subject matter jurisdiction of the legislative body, provided that no action
shall be taken on any item not appearing on the agenda unless the action is otherwise
authorized by subdivision (b) of Section 54954.2 [section omitted].

(b) (1) The legislative body of a local agency may adopt reasonable regulations to ensure
that the intent of the subdivision (a) is carried out, including, but not limited to, regulations
limiting the total amount of time allocated for public testimony on particular issues and for
each individual speaker.
  (2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), when the legislative body of a local agency limits
time for public comment, the legislative body of a local agency shall provide at least twice
the allotted time to a member of the public who utilizes a translator to ensure that non-

Planning Commission  Thursday, April 10, 2025
 English speakers receive the same opportunity to directly address the legislative body of
a local agency.”

In furtherance of Section 54954.3 of the Brown Act, the public is allotted to speak a total
of two (2) minutes on the entirety of the Consent Calendar, Appointment(s), with two (2)
minutes on each Public Hearing, and, if desired, an additional two (2) minutes on items
not on the agenda that are within the subject matter jurisdiction of the Planning
Commission. As specified in the Brown Act, a speaker utilizing a translator will receive
twice the amount of time specified.

4.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS: Now is the time for public participation on items listed on
  the Consent Calendar Items. Each speaker is allotted two (2) minutes in total for the
  entirety of the above sections.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  All matters listed under the Consent Calendar will be enacted by one motion unless an
  item(s) is pulled by the Planning Commission, in which case the item(s) will be removed
  from the Calendar and will be considered separately following this portion of the Agenda.

6.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

  6.A  Adopt Resolution No. PC-2025-002 approving Variance 25-0001, Conditional Use

  establish a mining and reclamation operation, including aggregate processing and
  a batch plant facility, on an approximately 80-acre site located on the northeast
  corner of the future alignment of East Avenue S and 80th Street East and adopt
  the Mitigated Negative Declaration and Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting
  Program prepared for the project.
  Memo Reso. No. PC-2025-002

  6.B  Adopt Resolution No. PC-2025-009, a Resolution of the Planning Commission of

 6.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

  6.A  Adopt Resolution No. PC-2025-010, a Resolution of the Planning Commission
  of the City of Palmdale, approving Tentative Parcel Map 84606, a request to
  subdivide a 13.77-acre parcel into two parcels located at the northwest corner of
  Rancho Vista Boulevard and Division Street and find that the project is
  categorically exempt from environmental review.

  Ivan Galeazzi, Associate Planner, presented this item and noted that both he and the
  applicant were present and available for this discussion.

  Chair Henderson opened the public hearing.

  No comments received.

  Chari Henderson closed the public hearing.

  Motion: Adopt Resolution No. PC-2025-010; as amended.
  Moved by: Commissioner Lujan, seconded by Vice Chair Elize
  Vote: Motion carried 4-1
  Yes: Chair Henderson, Vice Chair Elize, Commissioners, Lujan, Olivarez
  No: 0
  Abstain: 0
  Absent: 1

  6.B  Adopt Resolution No. PC-2025-006, a Resolution of the Planning Commission of
  the City of Palmdale approving Conditional Use Permit 24-0016, a request to
  establish a Smoke Shop within an existing commercial tenant space located at
  39904 10th Street West, Suite A, and find that the project is categorically
  exempt from environmental review.

  Ivan Galeazzi, Associate Planner, presented this item and noted that both he and the
  applicant were present and available for discussion.

  Staff and Commissioners discussed a concern with the safety and security to minors.

  Applicant Antwan Karabet Masrelian addressed the commission, assuring that a security
  plan would be implemented to monitor the premises 24 hours a day. Additionally, a floor
  plan will include measures to alleviate theft as well as prevent access to anyone under 18
  years of age.

  Chair Henderson opened the public hearing.

  No comments received.

  Chari Henderson closed the public hearing.
 PC Minutes 3.13.2025

  Motion: Adopt Resolution No. PC-2025-006
  Moved by: Commissioner Lujan, seconded by Vice Chair Elize
  Vote: Motion carried 3-1-1
  Yes: Chair Henderson, Vice Chair Elize, Commissioners, Lujan
  No: Commissioner Olivarez
  Abstain: 0
  Absent: 1

  6.C  Adopt Resolution No. PC-2025-005, a Resolution of the Planning Commission of
  the City of Palmdale, denying Variance 24-0001 and Minor Site Plan Review 24-
  0012; a request to add 144 square feet to an existing commercial building
  operating as a convenience market and a legal non-conforming fueling station
  located at 960 East Palmdale Boulevard (Kwik Serv Market).

  Assistant Planner, Juan Lopez, presented this item and noted that both he and the
  applicant were present and available for discussion.

  Tom Steeno, the project architect, opposed the staff's recommendation to deny the
  proposed project. The applicant claimed the staff report provided did not include
  findings to justify their recommendation.

  Staff and Commissioners ensued discussions related to findings, which are listed in
  Resolution Section 2; A through G. supporting the recommendation. Additionally, staff
  advised the applicant of the Commission’s procedural process, in which the option to
  adopt as presented, make a recommendation to continue the item, or schedule it to a
  future date to allow further review; furthermore, of his right to appeal the Commission’s
  decision.

  Chair Henderson opened the public hearing.

  No comments received.

  Chari Henderson closed the public hearing.

  Motion: Adopt Resolution No. PC-2025-005
  Moved by: Commissioner Olivarez, seconded by Commissioner Lujan
  Vote: Motion carried 3-1-1
  Yes: Chair Henderson, Vice Chair Elize, Commissioners Lujan
  No: Commissioner Olivarez
  Abstain: 0
  Absent: 1

  Public testimony received by Ms. Strout related to recent improvements and renovations
  to the roundabouts, and recent flooding in the Courson area and the vicinity of the gas
  station located at 10th Street East and Palmdale Blvd.

  The Planning Commission directed staff to reach out to follow up with Ms. Strout related
  to the traffic concerns.

  Chair Henderson closed public comments.

 8. STAFF COMMUNICATIONS

  Planning Manager Magaña announced that the City Council will be deciding on the
  modification to the Planning Commission meeting time on March 18, 2025. If adopted, the
  meeting of April 10th will be held at 5:00 p.m.

 9. COMMISSIONER REPORTS,  ANNOUNCEMENTS  AND  REQUESTS  FOR
  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  Commissioner Lujan congratulated the hard work and dedication of teachers and
  students of the Aerospace Academy Science Olympia team on their second-place
  finish in the Antelope Valley for the State Competition at Cal Tech on April 12, 2025,
  and to the Robotics Team #5012, which placed seventh out of 52 teams in the
  Ventura County Competition.

 10. ADJOURN

  Chair Henderson adjourned the Planning Commission meeting at 7:48 p.m. to Thursday,
  April 10, 2025, at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber, located at 38300 Sierra
  Highway, Suite B, Palmdale, California.

  PASSED, APPROVED, and ADOPTED this 10th day of April 2025.

  Dean Henderson, Chair
